partners.mechanism_chain: BCS1L (HGNC:1304) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial protein folding and assembly; HSCB (HGNC:4967) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial protein folding and assembly; Mitochondrial protein folding and assembly —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial complex III assembly; Mitochondrial protein folding and assembly —LEADS_TO→ Heme biosynthesis; Mitochondrial complex III assembly —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial complex III deficiency (HP:0003204); Heme biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Sideroblastic anemia (HP:0001911). Mutations in BCS1L (causing MONDO:0011308) and HSCB (causing MONDO:0030436) both impair the general process of mitochondrial protein folding and assembly. This shared impairment specifically affects the assembly of mitochondrial complex III, a key component of the electron transport chain, leading to mitochondrial complex III deficiency. Furthermore, proper mitochondrial function, supported by correct protein folding and assembly, is essential for efficient heme biosynthesis. Defects in heme biosynthesis, stemming from the compromised mitochondrial environment, result in sideroblastic anemia.
